title: Fold per-layer scale into inline requantizer; attention KV-cache compatibility
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: INT8 and FP8 paths pay a per-token cost for explicit scale/dequant round-trips in the attention kernel. This PR folds stable per-layer/chunk scaling factors into an inline requantizer inside the GEMM/attention kernels and adds compatibility glue for our attention KV-cache (so cached keys/values don't trigger extra conversions on read). Goals: reduce per-token arithmetic, improve single-stream latency, and keep cached tensors bit-compatible across quant/float fallbacks. Implementation summary: 1) introduce a lightweight FoldedScale descriptor that is emitted at model-load time and stored alongside quant metadata; 2) implement inline_requantizer.{cc,hh} which applies scale folding + rounding once on kernel entry and keeps activations in the requantized layout for the kernel duration; 3) modify attention KV load/store paths to check for FoldedScale and avoid redundant dequant->requant conversions when a cached shard already carries the folded scale tag; 4) add a guarded FP8 stochastic-round option (config flag) to preserve edge-case numerics for very small-scale layers; 5) update the continuous batcher to prefer grouping requests by compatible folded-scale signatures to maximize kernel reuse. Testing & benchmarks: unit tests added (tests/quant/scale_fold_test.cc) to validate numerical equivalence within target tolerances; end-to-end perf bench (bench/quant/bench_int8_fold.py) shows 8-14% single-stream latency reduction on A100-80GB with INT8 kernels and 6-9% throughput improvement in mixed-batch workloads when continuous batching groups by folded-scale. Backwards compatibility: when FoldedScale metadata is absent, kernels fall back to the previous explicit dequant/requant code path. Migration: model loader emits folded-scale for models that pass a short calibration pass; opt-out via REDWOOD_QUANT_NO_FOLD env var. Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked in Linear ENG-1289 - [x] Unit tests - [x] Perf benchmarks attached - [x] KV-cache compatibility glue - [x] Feature gated behind config flags and env opt-out - [x] Docs: docs/perf/quant-ops.md updated Notes: this is intentionally conservative — we avoid changing on-disk weight formats and only tag cache entries with a small folded-scale id. The approach aims to reduce runtime arithmetic without altering model fidelity. Related: ENG-1344 (continuous-batching grouping by quant-signature).

release_notes: Fold per-layer scales into an inline requantizer to reduce runtime arithmetic and improve INT8/FP8 kernel latency. Compatible with existing KV-cache through metadata tagging; feature is feature-gated and opt-out-able. Expect ~8-14% single-stream latency improvement on representative A100 INT8 workloads.
